capabilities: Play notes as audiobook-style chapters in a sidebar player
Save synthesized audio as MP3 files and embed them in notes
Switch between TTS providers and voices
Adjust playback speed, rewind, and repeat during playback
disambiguation: Not an audio recorder; it converts written note text to spoken audio rather than capturing microphone input.
extras: Deep provider setup (creating a dedicated AWS user, picking regions) and error help are moved to a separate Troubleshooting & Advanced Setup guide, not covered in this README.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in text-to-speech, so listening to your notes requires copying text into separate apps or services.

relations.evidence: Many services and self-hosted servers offer the same speech API as OpenAI.
Choose OpenAI-compatible as the provider to use one of them

requires.name: TTS provider credentials (AWS Polly, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google Cloud, Azure Speech, MiniMax)

summary: Text-to-speech plugin that reads notes aloud through an audiobook-style player, with multi-provider voices and MP3 saving for offline listening.
